title: Determine whether a child's submodule ignore setting hides grandchild dirt from committed-input admission
outcome: A real-Git probe establishes whether nested submodule ignore settings can hide changed grandchild input, and both projects receive the same supported conclusion.
acceptance: One real-Git fixture root -> child -> grandchild, with the child's committed .gitmodules setting submodule.<grandchild>.ignore=all and the grandchild edited, records what the existing rev 5 reader reports for root cleanliness, with a clean control. Include the child-local configuration variant if needed to distinguish Git precedence.

Record exact Git/input identities and command results. If dirt is hidden, file the follow-up remedy or explicit design decision within Greg's no-file-list rule and share the outcome with TermAl; do not silently declare the limitation accepted or bolt a new guard onto another changeset.
